subStrands.name: Government as Institution, Process and Field of Study

objectives.description: Government as an institution of the state: definition of state, features, structure and functions.
Government as a process or art of governing.
Government as an academic field of study – reasons for studying government.

strands.name: Basic Concepts and Principles of Government

objectives.description: Basic concepts – State, Society, Nation, Power, Authority, Legitimacy, Sovereignty, Democracy, Political Culture and Socialization, Communalism, Feudalism and oligarchy, Liberalism, Socialism, Communism, Capitalism, Fascism, Aristocracy, Totalitarianism – meaning and features.

Basic principles – Rule of Law, Fundamental Human Rights, Separation of Powers/Checks and Balances, Constitutionalism, Political participation, Representative Government, Centralization and Decentralization (Delegated Legislation, Devolution and Decentralization).
Definition and sources of constitutions.
Functions of constitutions.
Types and features of constitutions: Written and Unwritten, Rigid and Flexible.
The Executive – types, structure, composition/membership, functions, powers and limitations.
The Legislature – types, structure, composition/membership, functions, powers and limitations.
The Judiciary – types, structure, composition/membership, functions, powers and limitations; Judicial Independence.

strands.name: State Structure and Characteristics of Government

objectives.description: Types of state structure and government – Unitary, Federal, Confederal, Presidential or Non-parliamentary, Parliamentary or Cabinet, Monarchical and Republican: meaning, types, features, merits and demerits.
Citizenship: meaning, mode of acquisition, rights, duties and obligations of individuals in the state. Means of safeguarding rights of citizens.
Political Parties – definition, organization/structure, and functions.
Party Systems – definition, types, merits and demerits.

strands.name: Pressure Groups, Public Opinion and Mass Media

objectives.description: Pressure Groups – definition, types, mode of operation and functions.
Public opinion – definition, formation, measurement and importance.
Mass Media – definition, roles and impact.

strands.name: Electoral Systems, Processes and Electoral Management Body

objectives.description: Election – meaning and purpose of elections.
Franchise – meaning and limitations.
Types, advantages and disadvantages of Electoral Systems.
Electoral Management Body – definition, function, problems/constraints.
Public/Civil Service – meaning, structure, characteristics and functions.
Public/Civil Service Commission – meaning and functions.
Public Corporations – definition, purposes, functions, control, challenges, need for commercialization and privatization.
Local Governments – meaning, structure, purposes, functions, sources of revenue, control and problems.
The structural organization of pre-colonial political systems in Nigeria: Hausa/Fulani, the Yoruba and the Igbo.
The Policy and Structure of the British Colonial Administration – Crown Colony, Protectorate and Indirect Rule.
The Policy of French Colonial Administration – Assimilation and Association (Loi Cadre).
Impact, advantages and disadvantages of Colonial Rule.
Nationalism: meaning, factors and effects.
Key Nationalist leaders/movements and their contributions.
Nigeria pre-independence constitutions (features): Clifford 1922, Richards 1946, Macpherson 1951, Littleton 1954.

Nigeria post-independence constitutions (features): Independence Constitution 1960; Republican Constitution 1963; The 1979 and 1989 Constitutions; 1999 Constitution – origin, features, strength and weaknesses.
Development of major political parties in Nigeria: formation, objectives, sources of finance, achievements and failures.
Military rule in Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone, The Gambia and Liberia: causes, effects and various military regimes.

strands.name: Federal/Unitary Systems of Government in West Africa

objectives.description: Federal/Unitary systems of government in West Africa (Nigeria, Sierra Leone, The Gambia, Liberia): origin, factors, structure, features and problems.

subStrands.name: Foreign Policies of West African Countries

objectives.description: Foreign policies of Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone, The Gambia and Liberia: definitions, factors, objectives, advantages and disadvantages.
The United Nations Organization (UNO) – origin, aims/objectives, achievements and problems.
The Commonwealth of Nations – origin, aims/objectives, achievements and problems.
African Union (AU) – NEPAD: origin, aims/objectives, achievements and problems.
The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) – origin, aims/objectives, achievements and problems.
